mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.0%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) indicate a tightening cycle with rising real interest rates, suppressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0 and CPIAUCSL > 3.0.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment rates (UNRATE > 4.0%) reflect weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 50% of periods when UNRATE > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rates (UNRATE < 3.5%) signal a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 50% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing market activity (HOUST > 1300) indicates robust consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 50% of periods when HOUST > 1300.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneously high housing starts (HOUST > 1300) and retail sales (RSAFS > 500000) reflect strong consumer spending and economic momentum, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 50% of periods when HOUST > 1300 and RSAFS > 500000.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 50% of periods during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%).
